verdicts.rationale: The introduction explicitly identifies pixel-level limitations and inadequate assessment by VQA and visual grounding.
HLMAT is explicitly formulated as a multi-step MDP using textual coordinates without specialized architectures or implicit tokens.
The framework describes the composite visual input, task and target prompt, textual action output, and segmentation update using action history.
The trajectory generator uses mask error regions and explicitly applies all three stated filtering and stopping rules.
StaR+ explicitly retains reward-increasing actions, corrects decreasing actions with Fsim, and merges trajectories for fine-tuning.
The PRM description and Algorithm 2 specify current-state mIoU prediction, candidate sampling and scoring, and selection of the best mask across steps.
The dataset descriptions confirm the RES components, HRES provenance and subsets, and all stated DIS5K counts.
The evaluation protocol explicitly gives cIoU and the stated T and K settings for both datasets.
All four scores and their dataset splits match Table 1.
Section 5.4 reports the single-round StaR+ scores and the stated PRM and additional search improvements with the same comparators.
Both models' four annotation-filtering metrics match Table 3 exactly.
The limitations section identifies both failure modes and explicitly attributes the main bottleneck to fine-grained pixel localization.
The paper states that limited trajectory diversity constrains robustness and generalization, and that noisy masks cause erroneous actions near trajectory endpoints.
The search discussion names BFS and MCTS as more complex alternatives and leaves their exploration to future work because of the computation–performance trade-off.
The contribution list explicitly presents HLMAT, automatically trained SegAgent, and HRES for complex vision-centered multi-step research.
